name: BabyVelvet
summary: A lightweight reimplementation of the Velvet short-read assembler in Codon, built for the UVic CSC427 project rather than a weekly assignment: it constructs a de Bruijn graph, concatenates nodes, clips short tips and resolves bubbles through a tourbus module. The report describes Codon as a domain-extensible compiler and DSL framework with Python's syntax and semantics, chosen so the assembler reads like Python while running at C or C++ speed. The whole implementation is .py, run through the same Codon 0.19.3 CI harness as the rest of the course.
why_codon: The report states Codon gives the readability of Python while achieving performance similar to low-level languages such as C or C++.
note: The most substantial piece of CSC427 work found, and the only one carrying a poster and a written report. Named differently from the other student repos, so it would be missed by a name-based sweep of the course.

name: CSC427 Fall 2025 (oliwhitla)
summary: Coursework for UVic's Fall 2025 CSC427 bioinformatics course, running the full six weeks. Every Codon port is a .py file named for it -- tree_codon.py, nj_codon.py, upgma_codon.py in the phylogenetics week, utils_codon.py in week one -- so the repository carries no .codon file at all.
why_codon: Course requirement. Inferred from the paired Python and Codon versions of each algorithm and the course evaluation script that prints a runtime comparison between them.

name: CSC427 Fall 2025 (yushannn)
summary: Coursework for UVic's Fall 2025 CSC427 bioinformatics course, two weeks in. The Codon work is .py -- utils_codon.py in week one and a bio_codon package in week two -- and the week-one directory also keeps four codon_data logs, the recorded output of the timed runs the assignment asks for.
why_codon: Course requirement, and the committed codon_data logs are the timing output of the comparison the course asks students to run.

name: CSC427 Fall 2025 (kaceythai)
summary: Coursework for UVic's Fall 2025 CSC427 bioinformatics course, with a bio_codon motifs package in week two and a Leptospira project directory alongside the weekly work. Carries a nested copy of the course repository as well as a per-week workflow, so the same harness appears twice.
why_codon: Course requirement. Inferred from the bio_codon package and the shared evaluation harness that the Codon port is compared against the Python original.

name: CSC427 Fall 2025 (marlodenis)
summary: Coursework for UVic's Fall 2025 CSC427 bioinformatics course, one week deep: the genome-assembly assignment with its data, evaluation script and report. The smallest of the twelve student repositories and the earliest to stop.
why_codon: Course requirement. Inferred from week one's evaluate.sh, which runs the Python and Codon versions of the assembler and prints their runtimes.

name: oop-python-nycu
summary: Course material for object-oriented Python at NYCU, whose Python-compiler chapter times the same MIT OpenCourseWare Fibonacci example through CPython, Nuitka, Codon and PyPy inside a prepared Docker image. Codon is introduced for its parallelism and multithreading support through OpenMP and LLVM IR, and the chapter points at the group's own fork of the compiler rather than upstream.
why_codon: The chapter introduces Codon as better supporting parallelism and multithreading via OpenMP and LLVM IR, and runs it timed against the other Python compilers on the same example.
note: The chapter links ARG-NCTU/codon, a fork of the compiler held by the same group. Not yet opened; a candidate for the next pass.

name: oop-python-nycu-main
summary: A student's copy of the NYCU object-oriented Python course material, carrying the same Python-compiler chapter and its Codon section.
why_codon: Carries the course chapter unchanged, which introduces Codon for OpenMP and LLVM IR support and times it against the other Python compilers.
